## 6143c7ef56be

**Finding type: reproduced lesson shortcut; target left unchanged.**

A legal consecutive four-sample window exists at `difficulty="easy"`, `seed=158`, sample indices `0..3`. The first three layouts are all `corners`; the fourth is `independent`. The rival “read the four outer grid-corner colors and write them into the former cyan 2x2 in TL/TR/BL/BR order” matches the selected Racket authority on all three demonstrations but fails the query. All four inputs pass the target validator. The supported Racket apply used rule hash `9c659fa323b2`, matching the catalog, and generator hash `5ec5e6e56df63dfacb99b052b2d333b94d730c48fe0a099f2a3aa44d112b9045`.

Evidence: `checks/audit/6143c7ef56be/counterexample.json`, input `checks/audit/6143c7ef56be/input.json`, and authority receipt `checks/audit/6143c7ef56be/racket.json`. This is a lesson-assembly risk, not a claim that every production lesson uses same-seed consecutive indices. A schedule or lesson-level rival gate would remove the ambiguity.

A separate portable-test issue was reproduced: the task-test stage reported 35 passed / 3 failed. Two failures use a test-relative canonical-data path that does not exist in the copied runtime; the retained root fixture also compares authority text byte-for-byte and fails on formatting-only differences. Evidence: `checks/audit-6143c7ef56be-task_tests.log`. The generator itself passed the completed lint, self-check, and rule-smoke stages before the audit battery was interrupted; no source was modified.
